newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says new bonds to replace Brady discounts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says new bonds to replace Brady discounts.

text.p: The $1.0 billion worth of new 20-year bonds that the United Mexican States placed on Tuesday will replace Brady bonds with a nominal value of $1.24 billion, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.
"The funds coming from this placement will be used to pay off discount bonds issued by the Federal government as part of its debt restructuring deal of 1989-1992," the Ministry said.
Market analysts reported good demand for the new 20-year bonds. The amount initially offered, $750 million, was increased to $1.0 billion.
The new bond will pay 445 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, which is down from the 552 basis points spread the 30-year bonds issued in May were floated at.
The Finance Ministry said the bond deal will allow the government to capture the difference between the nominal value of the Brady bonds and their market value, at a savings of about $240 million.
"The cancellation of the discount (Brady) bonds will allow the recuperation of associated collateral worth about $410 million. These funds will be applied to pay off short-term debt," it said.
The Ministry said the operation will allow it to cut about $650 million from its external public debt. The discount bonds, which had a 30-year term, are secured by zero-coupon bonds.
